I been working this land since before most my neighbors was born. My sons go to town for work now, so it is mostly me and the old woman. The big boy helps when he can. I have 15 mu, but I do not plant cotton on all of it no more — cotton takes too much picking and my back is not what it was. So I keep about 3 mu for cotton on the sandy patch near the road where wheat does not do so well anyway. The other 12 mu I do wheat then maize, same as always, same as everybody here.

For the wheat I plant in October after the maize comes off. I use the seed the dealer sells — Jimai something, I forget the number, but my neighbor Lao Wang had a good crop with it last year so I buy the same. Before planting I spread one bag of diammonium per mu, that is 50 jin, no wait, 100 jin, one big bag. Then after the spring green-up I give it one bag of urea per mu when I flood-irrigate. I water four times — once before winter so it does not freeze dry, once in spring, once when the stalks stand up, once when the grain is filling. I spray two times, once for the weeds and once when the little green bugs come. I run the rotary tiller after maize, cannot plough deep no more, the small tractor does not pull it.

For the maize I plant right into the wheat stubble in June, do not till, just poke it in with the seeder. Neighbors all do this now. I buy Zhengdan or whatever the dealer pushes. I put half a bag compound fertilizer per mu when I plant and one bag urea per mu when it is knee-high. Water two, three times depending on the rain. Spray once for the borer.

Cotton is more trouble. I plant in late April. Cotton eats a lot, so I give it more — one and a half bag diammonium per mu before planting, then urea twice during the season, maybe 60 jin total. Must spray many times, five or six, the bollworm comes every year. Water three, four times from the well.

I do not change much year to year. When I change something and it goes bad, that is a whole year gone. Better to do what worked.
